summary: Comments on RFC 123 from MIT Project MAC. Requiring exactly 32 bits for the first connection is hard for some 36-bit machines such as their PDP-10. They suggest letting the server send more bits, filled with nulls, with an 8-bit byte size.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 148 comments on the Initial Connection Protocol in RFC 123. It suggests a way for 36-bit machines to handle the required 32-bit initial data by sending a larger padded amount.

subtitle: A comment on the 32-bit data-size requirement for the Initial Connection Protocol.

tldr.problem: RFC 123's 32-bit byte-size requirement for the initial connection was difficult for some 36-bit machines to handle.
tldr.mechanism: A. Bhushan suggests allowing the server to send more than 32 bits, using null fillers for the remainder, and setting the connection byte size to 8 bits.
tldr.outcome: RFC 148 updates RFC 123 with a suggestion; the text does not say whether it was adopted.

today: RFC 148 updates RFC 123 with a comment on its initial-connection requirement. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that updates or replaces RFC 148.

sections.title: The 32-Bit Requirement
sections.content:
RFC 123 requires the byte size s to be 32 bits for the initial connection. A. Bhushan says this creates difficulty for some 36-bit machines, including the PDP-10 NCP at MIT Project MAC.

That NCP can transmit data in 36-bit bytes in image mode or 8-bit characters in ASCII mode, but cannot send or receive exactly 32 bits.
sections.plainLanguage: The PDP-10 handles data in 36-bit or 8-bit pieces, not exactly 32 bits. That makes the initial-connection requirement difficult for this machine.

sections.title: The Proposed Adjustment
sections.content: Bhushan suggests allowing the server to send more than 32 bits, for example 72 bits, with the remaining bits filled by nulls. He also suggests setting the connection byte size s to 8 bits.
sections.plainLanguage: The suggestion is to send a larger amount and fill the extra bits with nulls, using an 8-bit byte size.

sections.title: A Comment, Not a Revised Protocol
sections.content: RFC 148 is a short comment on RFC 123. It proposes a change to the initial-connection requirement but does not provide revised protocol text or say whether the suggestion was adopted.
sections.plainLanguage: This is a suggestion about RFC 123, not a new protocol specification. The note does not report whether the change was accepted.

references.text: The RFC being commented on, RFC 123.
